headlines.text: 2023 brought us this moment: history was made as Orange Cassidy vs. Jeff Jarrett contested the very first AEW International Title match, appearing on Dynamite, rated 6.42. In the final defense of the AEW All-Atlantic Championship before its rebrand, Cassidy fought off interference from Jarrett's entire crew to retain and become the first-ever AEW International Champion.

2026 brought us this moment: MJF vs. Adam Page went to battle over the AEW World Heavyweight Title in a Texas Death Match, appearing on Revolution, rated 8.98 ? a match that lived up to every bit of hype. It marked Adam Page's 20th match with the title on the line. In an unhinged Texas Death Match with Page's very ability to ever challenge for the title again on the line, MJF survived a savage ten-count brawl to retain the AEW World Championship.
It was 2024 when it marked the first-ever meeting between Konosuke Takeshita and Komander on Rampage, rated 7.62 ? a well-worked match.

secondaries.text: Back on this day in 2025, Dante Martin stepped back through the curtain after just over 2 months away, appearing on Collision.

On a Sunday in 2026, back when Jon Moxley vs. Konosuke Takeshita fought tooth and nail for the AEW Continental Title, appearing on Revolution, rated 8.68 ? an incredible outing. It was the 20th time the AEW Continental Title had been on the line, a nice marker in that championship's story. In a first-ever No Time Limit meeting, Moxley choked out Takeshita with a grapevine rear naked choke to retain the Continental Title in a war that took every ounce of both men.

Rewind to 2026, when FTR vs. The Young Bucks put the AEW World Tag Team Titles on the line, appearing on Revolution, rated 9.17 ? an outstanding performance from both sides. FTR retained the AEW World Tag Team Titles over the Young Bucks with an Avalanche Shatter Machine, the veterans once again proving too much for the EVPs.
